# Scope cutting

A backlog needs pruning the way an orchard does. Features that nobody asked about for months are dead wood: they still take attention, still appear in every planning, and compete with the work that bears fruit. Cutting back is uncomfortable, but it redirects the team's vigour towards the few branches that matter.

My rule: at the start of each quarter I go through the list and remove anything older than six months that has no owner and no customer. The remaining items get more room and more care. Pruning also protects the schedule, because a smaller scope is easier to finish.

Cut back early, and cut hard, rather than late and in panic.
